data.why: the repo ships the full pre-computed pipeline output (carbon_cells.parquet, district_summary.json, model_metrics.json, ndvi_monthly.json) under IIRS/Carbon_Stocks/results/ plus the Flask frontend assets under IIRS/Carbon_Stocks/carbon_project/frontend/, all committed as real git blobs (not LFS), so the Streamlit app reads them directly with no uploads or synthetic data needed.

goals: find the total soil organic carbon stock and crop carbon flux estimated for the district
click into an individual 250 m grid cell to inspect its soil carbon, crop NPP flux, elevation, slope and data-source flags
compare the random forest model's spatial cross-validation accuracy (R²) for NPP and SOC predictions
check how well the model's 90% prediction intervals are calibrated (coverage) to judge whether the uncertainty estimates are trustworthy
search, filter and export cells via the Explorer page for further analysis
see how the two independent crop carbon estimation methods compare against MODIS NPP

review.summary: The tree states clearly what this dashboard is for (district SOC stock and crop carbon flux, their uncertainty and cross-checks, model trust, per-cell inspection and export), and every one of the 13 screens I opened backs its node exactly. It needs light restructuring before filing: t5 is under the wrong phase, t14 is navigation written as a task, t17 combines two tasks, f6 is too big and f2 overlaps f1, and it is missing a task and feature for the scope-and-caveats notes.
